Introduction

The Challenge: Art vs. Code ""Gabi"" is a beloved illustrated character created by Marie-Hortense Camous, representing the culture of Nice. The author had a very specific vision: she didn't want a standard grid-based website. She wanted the site to feel like opening one of her books full of sprawling, hand-drawn landscapes.

The Solution I partnered with the author to act as the bridge between art and technology. While she provided the artistic direction and page illustrations, my role was to translate those static, pixel-perfect drawings into a fluid, responsive website that works on every screen size.

Responsive Adaptation

Preserving the Composition Translating full-page illustrations into the web is notoriously difficult. A standard responsive behavior would often crop the image awkwardly or hide key details on smaller screens.

To solve this, I meticulously calibrated the background positioning and scale for every breakpoint. Instead of a ""one-size-fits-all"" crop, I adjusted the alignment of the illustrations to ensure Gabi and the iconic landscapes remained the focal point, whether viewed on a wide monitor or a smartphone.

Technical Architecture

The ""Headless-Lite"" Approach The client needed e-commerce functionality but wanted to avoid the high monthly fees and rigid templates of a full Shopify store. I engineered a hybrid solution:

  1. Build: I developed the frontend in Webflow for total design freedom.
  2. Host: I exported the code to self-host it. This strategy eliminated recurring monthly platform fees, providing a highly cost-effective solution for the client without sacrificing quality
  3. Commerce: I integrated Shopify Buy Buttons. This injects a secure, world-class checkout system directly into the custom design, offering the best of both worlds.
","

Performance

Heavy Visuals, Light Code Websites rich in illustrations often suffer from slow load times. Through aggressive asset optimization and clean HTML/CSS export, I achieved near-perfect scores on Google PageSpeed Insights.

This proves that you don't have to sacrifice creativity for performance. The site is accessible, SEO-friendly, and loads instantly.

Introduction

The Challenge: Why do we quit what we start? We live in the golden age of self-education, yet completing a course or mastering a new hobby remains incredibly difficult. The enthusiasm is there, but the structure is missing.

The Solution: SkillTrack is a mobile learning companion designed to fix the consistency gap. By combining habit-tracking mechanics with gamification, it turns the chaotic process of self-study into a rewarding, structured journey.

Research &
column2:
Discovery

Understanding the Learner’s Struggle: I kicked off the project with a simple question: What stops people from learning? Through a mix of surveys and 1:1 interviews, I dug into user habits.

The data revealed a clear pattern: motivation isn’t the problem consistency is. Users felt overwhelmed by unorganized resources and lacked the immediate feedback loops that make learning addictive.

  • The Career Climber: Needs efficiency and measurable progress to upskill for work.
  • The Curious Learner: Needs a fun, low-pressure way to explore creative hobbies.

Despite their different goals, both needed the same thing: accountability.

Surrounding this are the Learning Hub (where resources live) and the Profile (where achievements are celebrated).

Localization

Designing for Global Users (LTR &
column3:
RTL): SkillTrack is designed to be accessible in both Left-to-Right (English) and Right-to-Left (Arabic/Hebrew) languages. However, I avoided blindly mirroring every single element.

The Strategy: Adaptive Content, Fixed Navigation: While I mirrored the visual flow of text, progress bars, and directional icons to match the natural reading order of RTL users, I made a strategic decision to keep the Bottom Navigation consistent in both versions.‍

Why? To preserve muscle memory. The thumb learns where key actions live. By anchoring the core navigation in the same spot, I ensure that the physical interaction remains familiar, even if the language settings change.

Reflections

What I Learned: SkillTrack taught me that gamification is a delicate balance. It’s not just about slapping badges on a screen
column2:
it’s about creating meaningful feedback loops that make the user feel accomplished.

Next Steps: If I were to continue developing this product, I would introduce Social Accountability features. Allowing users to share milestones with friends could be the final piece of the puzzle to solve the motivation problem.

Introduction

The Challenge: Smart Enseignes has been crafting luxury signage for hotels and boutiques in Nice, Cannes, and Monaco since 1979. However, their previous website didn't reflect the premium quality of their physical work.

The Goal: They needed a complete digital overhaul. The goal was to build a site that felt less like a brochure and more like a high-end catalogue one that would immediately distinguish them from competitors who were stuck with outdated, clunky websites.

Design &
column2:
Adaptation

Expanding the Visual System: I started with a specific art direction dark backgrounds to let the neon and metal work ""pop."" While I had a few initial UI screens to work from, my role was to expand this style into a comprehensive design system.

I designed the remaining layouts to ensure consistency, creating a mood that feels industrial yet elegant. The result is a seamless experience where the digital interface recedes, allowing the colorful product photography to take center stage.

Webflow Development

Empowering the Client with CMS: A portfolio site is useless if it's hard to update. I utilized Webflow's CMS to build a dynamic ""Realizations"" gallery.

  • Advanced Filtering: I implemented a custom search bar and filtering system, allowing potential clients to instantly sort through years of work to find exactly what they need (e.g., ""Neon,"" ""Metal,"" or ""Interior"").
  • Client Autonomy: I set up the backend structure so the team at Smart Enseignes can upload new projects, photos, and descriptions in minutes without needing to touch a line of code.

Performance &
column3:
Compliance

Fast, Visible, and Legal: A high-end website needs to perform as well as it looks.

  • Speed &
column4:
SEO: Through careful asset optimization and clean code structure, I achieved top-tier Google PageSpeed scores. This technical foundation helped the site rank highly for local keywords in the Riviera region.
  • GDPR Adherence: I implemented a fully compliant cookie consent system and privacy structure. I ensured the site adheres to strict EU data regulations without cluttering the UI or disrupting the user experience with intrusive pop-ups.

Introduction

The Challenge: Clarity in Politics: Ewan Corinaldesi is running for mayor of Roquefort-les-Pins in 2026. In local elections, the biggest hurdle isn't just having good ideas, it's getting those ideas across clearly. He needed a platform that felt personal, professional, and accessible to every generation of voter.

The Solution: I designed and built choisirroquefort.fr as the central hub for his campaign. It’s more than just a biography
column2:
it’s a living manifesto designed to present his team, his vision, and his program without the visual clutter often found in political sites.

Design &
column3:
Branding

From Logo to Design System: The campaign team provided a logo, but they needed a full digital identity. I expanded their existing branding into a cohesive UI system.

  • Trust-First UI: I prioritized whitespace and legible typography to ensure the candidate's message was easy to read, whether for a first-time voter or a senior citizen.
  • Navigation Strategy: The site structure is intentionally flat. I wanted voters to find the ""Project"" (Program) and ""Team"" sections in a single click, reducing friction between interest and information.

Webflow Development

Built for Agility &
column4:
Action: A political campaign needs to move fast and capture momentum.

  • Autonomy (CMS): I built custom back-end collections for News and Team Members, allowing the staff to publish updates instantly without needing to touch a line of code.
  • Fundraising Integration: I seamlessly integrated Donorbox to handle campaign donations. This turned the site into a secure fundraising tool, allowing supporters to contribute in seconds without navigating away from the branded experience.

Service &
column5:
Support

Reliable Post-Launch Care: I don't just deliver the code and disappear. I treat ongoing support as a standard part of my service.

Although the site is designed for autonomy, I remain fully available to assist the team. Whether they face a technical hurdle or need urgent help with a specific update, they know they can call me and get a quick resolution.

Responsive Experience

Campaigning in Your Pocket: Knowing that most constituents would access the site via social media links on their phones, I adopted a mobile-first approach.

The site is fully responsive, ensuring that long-form text (like the manifesto) remains readable on small screens, and the ""Join the Committee"" CTA is always within thumb's reach.

","

Impact

A Professional Standard &
column6:
Search Dominance: The website establishes immediate credibility. By moving away from generic templates, the campaign signals that they are serious, organized, and ready to lead.

The results speak for themselves: the site has achieved an average Google Search position of 2.8, with a massive 41.3% Click-Through Rate. This ensures that when voters search for local issues, they find the candidate's official platform first not rumors or news snippets.
